text:
Help me write an announcement to our staff. I'm the COO of a credit union with 7 branches. We're closing the Maple Street and Route 9 branches on March 31 and moving the people who work there to a new member phone and chat center.

Facts:
- The two branches have 14 staff between them. Every one of them is offered a job in the phone and chat center at the same pay or higher.
- Visits to those two branches fell 44% over the last three years. Phone and chat contacts across the credit union went up 60%.
- Members calling us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold.
- The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. The branches were open 9 to 5. Shifts will rotate.
- Staff in the center can work from home two days a week after 90 days of training.
- Anyone who doesn't take the new role gets 2 weeks of pay for every year they've worked here.

I want the announcement to say that this change will make everyone's job better. About 400 words, sent by email from me.

Before I draft, a few questions. The answers will change what goes in the email.

1. **Have the 14 people at Maple Street and Route 9 already been told in person?** If this email is how they find out, it needs to be written differently. Most people would also expect to hear news like this from their manager first, not by email to all staff.
2. **What are the dates?** When does the center open, where is it, and by what date must people accept the new role or take the severance? Staff will want a deadline and a location (their commute) before anything else.
3. **How do the rotating shifts work?** How often would someone work until 8 p.m.? Is there extra pay for evening shifts? This is the first thing staff who are used to 9 to 5 will ask about.
4. **What do they keep?** Do seniority, benefits and paid time off carry over? Is there a minimum or maximum on the severance, and does health coverage continue? Also, what decides who gets "higher" pay rather than the same pay?
5. **What happens to everyone else?** Does the center take calls off the other five branches, so their staff spend less time on the phone? Is anything changing for those branches? People at the other branches will wonder whether they're next.
6. **Who can people talk to?** Is there a named person, an all-staff meeting or a Q&A session I can point them to?

**On "this will make everyone's job better":** your facts back up part of this, but not all of it.

- **What they support:** members wait 9 minutes on hold, and the work is moving to phone and chat. The new role puts these 14 people where members now need them, at the same pay or more, with two days a week at home after training.
- **What they don't support:** the center is open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on rotating shifts. For someone who has worked 9 to 5 at a branch, evenings are a real cost, and some may simply prefer working face to face with members. "Better for everyone" also doesn't fit anyone who takes the severance.
- **How it might be read:** if the email says "better for everyone" and then mentions 8 p.m. shifts, the 14 will read it as spin, and they'll doubt the rest of the email too.

**What I'd suggest:** say plainly that this change protects every job and puts it where members need us. List what's better (pay, working from home, shorter hold times for members). State the evening shifts openly, next to whatever you tell me about how the rotation works or extra pay for those shifts.

If you'd still rather go with "better for everyone," I'll write it that way. It's your decision, since you know your staff. Also, is there anything they'll find out anyway that the email should address first, such as other branch closures being considered?

1. I don't know yet whether the 14 will have been told in person before this goes out.
2. The center is at our main office on Elm Avenue. Written offers go out by February 14, and decisions are due March 1. I don't know the center's opening date.
3. Staff with the most years here pick shifts first. I don't know how often someone would work until 8, or whether there's extra pay for evenings.
4. Pay in the center starts $1.50 an hour above current teller pay. Anyone who takes the new role and wants out within 6 months can still get the severance. I don't know about seniority, benefits, PTO, a severance cap, or health coverage.
5. I don't know.
6. Anyone who wants one can have a one-on-one meeting with HR.

On "better for everyone": you're right that it goes past what I can show. Say what's true instead.

On things they'll find out anyway: I don't know of other closures being considered. But our current phone team lost about 30% of its people last year, and people will know that.

Here's the draft. It doesn't say the change makes everyone's job better. It says what's true and states the costs openly: the evening shifts and the phone team's turnover.

<final_document>
**Subject: Maple Street and Route 9 branches will close March 31**

Team,

I'm writing to share a decision that affects all of us, and most directly our 14 colleagues at Maple Street and Route 9. Both branches will close on March 31. Everyone who works there will be offered a job in our new member phone and chat center, at the same pay or higher.

**Why we're doing this**

Members have changed how they reach us. Over the last three years, visits to these two branches fell 44%. Over the same period, phone and chat contacts across the credit union rose 60%. Members who call us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold. That's too long, and the people answering those calls have been handling more contacts every year. This move puts 14 experienced colleagues where members are now trying to reach us.

**What the new role looks like**

- The center is at our main office on Elm Avenue.
- Pay starts $1.50 an hour above current teller pay. No one will be offered less than they earn today.
- The center is open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. That's a longer day than the branches' 9-to-5 hours, and shifts will rotate, so some shifts will run into the evening. Staff with the most years here pick their shifts first.
- After 90 days of training, you can work from home two days a week.

**What happens next**

- Written offers go out by February 14.
- Decisions are due March 1.
- If you decide not to take the new role, you'll receive two weeks of pay for every year you've worked here.
- If you take the role and decide within six months that it isn't right for you, you can still leave with that same severance. You don't have to make a final decision before you've tried the job.

**Something I know is on people's minds**

Our phone team lost about 30% of its people last year. Many of you know that, and I won't pretend otherwise. Adding 14 experienced people makes that team substantially bigger. The six-month option means no one who joins it is locked in.

This decision covers these two branches. I don't know of any plans to close others.

**If you have questions**

Anyone who wants a one-on-one meeting with HR can have one. Please ask for it.

To everyone at Maple Street and Route 9: you've served members in those communities well, and that experience is exactly what members calling us need. I hope you'll join the center.

[Your name]
Chief Operating Officer
</final_document>

Before you send it:

- **Tell the 14 in person first if you can.** The draft works either way, but finding out from an all-staff email is hard on the people most affected.
- **Some things are left out because you don't know them yet:** the center's opening date, how often people would work until 8, whether evenings pay extra, and whether seniority, benefits, paid time off and health coverage carry over. People will ask about these in the HR meetings, so it's worth having the answers ready. If you get them before sending, add them under "What the new role looks like."
- **The line about other closures says what you told me:** you don't know of any. If you can state it more firmly, for example that no other closures are planned, staff at the other five branches will find that more reassuring.
- **Add your name** in the signature.
